title: Violet motif
subtitle: A five-petal violet in purple with a yellow centre, 6 cm
excerpt: The violet is a compact five-petal flower with two upper petals slightly smaller than the three lower petals, replicating the asymmetric real violet profile. Worked in 4-ply cotton on a 2.5 mm hook it measures 6 cm — small enough for a brooch backing, hairpin, or scatter motif on a shawl. In DK on a 4 mm hook it scales to 9 cm for cushion applique.
sourceNotes: Weldon's Practical Crochet, Volume 4 (1889), violet and small flower motif chapter (Internet Archive). Therese de Dillmont, Encyclopedia of Needlework (1886), crochet violet construction.
heroPrompt: A crochet violet motif in deep purple 4-ply cotton with a yellow French knot centre, 6 cm across, photographed flat on natural linen in soft daylight. Five petals, two upper slightly smaller.

chartDefinition.title: Violet motif
chartDefinition.caption: Magic ring centre. Five petals: 3 lower petals (ch-6 arches with 5htr fill) and 2 upper petals (ch-5 arches with 4htr fill) for asymmetry. Yellow French knot centre embroidered after.

glossaryTerms.definition: An adjustable starting loop that pulls closed to leave no visible centre hole. The violet petals all emerge from the same tight magic ring.

content.text: The violet builds all five petals directly from a
magic ring

of 10 dc. Three lower petals use a ch-6 arch filled with 5 htr; two upper petals use a ch-5 arch with 4 htr, making them slightly narrower. The asymmetry between the two petal sizes replicates the real violet's face shape. A yellow French knot at the centre completes the picture.

attrs.title: Materials for one motif
attrs.body: About 3 g of purple 4-ply cotton. A 2.5 mm hook. Tapestry needle. Yellow embroidery thread for the centre French knot. Scissors.

content.text: Gauge
Each finished violet motif measures 6 cm across in 4-ply cotton with a 2.5 mm hook.
Stitches used
chain (ch), slip stitch (sl st), magic ring (MR) — UK and US shared.
double crochet (dc) — UK; US "single crochet".
half treble (htr) — UK; US "half double crochet."
Pattern
Centre ring
Form a magic ring. Ch 1. 10dc into ring. Sl st to first dc to join. (10 dc.)
Lower petals — 3 times

Work 3 lower petals into alternate dc of the ring: *Ch 6. Into the ch-6 arch work 5htr. Sl st back into the ring dc you started from. Sl st into the next dc (skip 1dc).* Repeat from * to * twice more. (3 lower petals in 6 dc of the ring.)
Upper petals — 2 times
Work 2 upper petals into the remaining 4 dc: *Ch 5. Into the ch-5 arch work 4htr. Sl st back into the ring dc. Sl st into the next dc.* Repeat from * to * once. Fasten off.

definition.title: Violet motif
definition.caption: 10dc magic ring. Lower petals (x3): ch-6 arch, 5htr fill. Upper petals (x2): ch-5 arch, 4htr fill. Smaller upper petals create asymmetry.

content.text: Finishing
Embroider a yellow French knot at the very centre of the ring. Weave in ends. Sew the violet onto the base fabric or use as a brooch motif by attaching to a brooch backing.
Care
Handwash in cool water. Lay flat to dry. The petals retain their arch without blocking.
What to try next

The cherry blossom (crochet-flower-cherry-blossom) is the same five-petal scale with picot-edged petals for a lighter look. The daisy (crochet-daisy-basic) gives the same small-flower scale in a different construction.
